1	# Fake Bambu printer (in-process)
2	
3	Substitutes `FakeBambuAgent` for Bambu's closed network plugin so header menu,
4	Select Machine, and print can run without hardware. It is not a network fake:
5	MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented.
6	
7	The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
8	`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
9	fake unless asked.
10	
11	This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.
12	
13	## What success looks like
14	
15	- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
16	- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
17	- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
18	- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
19	  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.
20	
21	If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
22	fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.
23	
24	## Turn it on
25	
26	Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.
27	
28	`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:
29	
30	```json
31	"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
32	```
33	
34	JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
35	the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.
36	
37	Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
38	`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
39	`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
40	either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
41	`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
42	`orca`.
43	
44	**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
45	as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
46	Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
47	`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
48	`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
49	`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.
50	
51	Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
52	config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
53	is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.
54	
55	The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
56	**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.
57	
58	## Drive state
59	
60	Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
61	fake rereads it about once a second.
62	
63	```json
64	{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
65	```
66	
67	| Field | Meaning |
68	|---|---|
69	| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
70	| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
71	| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
72	| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
73	| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |
74	
75	No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
76	field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
77	tray per spool, up to 4:
78	
79	```json
80	{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
81	```
82	
83	`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
84	when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
85	saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
86	spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
87	`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
88	`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
89	id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
90	draws no swatch for it.
91	
92	Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.
93	
94	## Print
95	
96	Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
97	The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.
98	
99	If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
100	menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
101	scenario after send.
102	
103	## Isolate a running app (agents)
104	
105	Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.
106	
107	On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
108	a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
109	`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
110	`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.
111	
112	Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
113	posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
114	half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
115	title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
116	for Print.
117	
118	Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
119	use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.
120	
121	## Unit tests
122	
123	`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
124	control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
125	test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.
126	
127	## Agent id
128	
129	Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
130	id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.

input.content:
# Calibration in JusPrin: what was built and how it was checked

Written 2026-10-21 for someone who has not followed the work. The branch is
`claude/calibration` in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/calibration`. Nothing
has been pushed. This report, the brief and the handoff are untracked on
purpose.

## The short version

A person can now ask JusPrin to calibrate a filament. They can do it in
three ways: from the printer chip, from a filament slot, or from a printer
card on Home. Or they can just describe a print problem in the chat. The
assistant asks which test fits and makes one of three OrcaSlicer tests as a
project of its own: a temperature tower, the flow-ratio test, or a
pressure-advance tower. It slices the test and sends it to the printer, then
reads the person's photo of the result. It saves the best value into a named
copy of the filament ("Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1M · Fake A1 mini calibrated"),
never into OrcaSlicer's stock preset.

Everything was built and tested on the Windows machine only. macOS and Linux
were not built or run.

## What was built, commit by commit

1. **53d0fc4f4a — the `calibration_generate` tool.** The tool takes the test
   and its range, then does three things:
   - saves and closes the open project the same way opening a project does;
   - calls OrcaSlicer's own generator for that test;
   - reports what it made: the project name, the test objects, the range
     actually applied, and a sentence the assistant can repeat.

   It is offered both in the app and over MCP (your answer to question 2).

   Supporting changes in the same commit:
   - The workspace now says whether the open plate is a calibration test and
     what its steps are. This is seam (a), the one you chose.
   - When a save would also save changes the person had not saved yet, the
     message now names each one with its saved value. The assistant can then
     put the saved value back.
   - One small addition to an OrcaSlicer-owned file: `Plater::set_project_name`,
     a public forwarder to the private setter. A simulated rebase onto
     upstream 1bc39fd358 merged it with no conflicts.

2. **bab11c8eb1 — the calibration skill.** `AgentUI/src/skills/calibration/SKILL.md`
   tells the assistant several things:
   - when a test is worth making;
   - the two facts to confirm first, with a "Make the test / Not now" choice;
   - how to read each test's photo, and how to name and save the result.

   When the person is already on their own preset, the assistant asks whether
   to write into it or save a copy (your answer to question 1). The
   print-issues skill gained one line pointing to this skill.

3. **c15aecfc5e — the three Calibrate… rows.**
   - The rows are on the printer chip menu, the filament slot menu and the
     Home card's menu.
   - Each one shows OrcaSlicer's `MessageDialog` first. The dialog names the
     project that will be saved and closed, and says the test's settings are
     temporary.
   - Then the row opens the project chat with a message in the person's
     voice. The assistant asks which test.
   - From a Home card, the skill has the assistant set that printer up first.

4. **196daa08de — the tool guide.** The calibration table in
   `mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` now describes one tool, not two.

5. **be98979009 — a crash fix found by the end-to-end run.** Driving the tool
   over MCP crashed the app.
   - **Cause:** opening the test's project clears the list of tool calls,
     which can move the calibration call's own record in memory. The code
     then read that record after the move.
   - **Fix:** it now reads what it needs first. The same mistake in the
     tool-running loop is also fixed.
   - **Test:** a new bridge test fails without the fix and passes with it.
   - **Also in this commit:** the tool's result no longer repeats OrcaSlicer's
     "outside the build volume" notice. That notice is about the full-height
     tower before the generator cuts it down.

6. **947fef989f — `--fake-printer` for the MCP test fixture.** The shell
   harness can now start its MCP fixture on a saved Bambu A1 mini that is
   connected to the in-process fake printer. The Testing README says how.

## What was checked, and how

| Check | Where | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Adapter harness: each of the three tests generated from a project with unsaved edits; the project was saved first; the new project is named; the plate holds the test; the print's settings match the request; a reopened test still reports its steps; saving into a named copy | `workspace_adapter_integration_harness`, Windows | All 15 calibration checks pass. One unrelated check fails, explained below |
| Contract tests for the range rules | `workspace_contract_tests` | All pass (44 cases) |
| Tool, MCP and skill tests | `agent_bridge_tests` | 382 of 383 pass. The failure was there before this work, explained below |
| Page tests: the skill is listed, readable, and under the size limit; the Home menu row; the protocol | Vitest (AgentUI, HomeUI) | Pass, apart from three line-ending failures that were there before |
| The three rows: each draws, shows the dialog, Cancel leaves the project untouched, Start opens the chat and the test project | `shell_integration_harness --calibration-capture`, real menu clicks | Pass, 0 failures |
| End to end over MCP on the fake Bambu printer: refused range; temperature tower made; workspace reports its steps; tower sliced; stock filament refused; saved as the named copy; a second save updates the same copy (exactly one exists); pressure-advance tower with the default range; the test's own setting change named with its saved value and left out of the copy | `--manual-mcp --fake-printer` with the stdio bridge `jusprin-mcp.exe` | 18 of 18 checks pass |

Screenshots for review are in `calibration-review/`:

- `step1/` shows each test from the adapter harness.
- `step3/` shows the rows and dialogs.
- `e2e-mcp/` has the end-to-end run, its full MCP transcript and the driver
  script.

In e2e-mcp shots 02 to 05, the 3D view and settings panel are grey because
they were captured mid-redraw. Shot 06 shows the final state at rest.

### Failures that have nothing to do with calibration

- **Adapter harness, `slice_failure_in_orca_words`.** The check looks for the
  English catalogue's wording ("is not suggested for use printing…"). This
  Windows run shows OrcaSlicer's source wording instead ("is not suggested
  to be used to print…"), so the catalogue is not loaded there. The check
  comes from the slice-failure work of 2026-10-18 (c7ed56d027). It failed the
  same way in every run today.
- **Bridge test line 1940 and three Vitest checks.** These compare text with
  `\n` line endings, and this Windows checkout has `\r\n`.
- **Default shell harness: 8 failures.** A baseline build of the commit this
  work started from (f323db81c7) gave the same 8 failures and 568 passes, so
  they are not caused by this work. The keyboard-menu checks among them are
  flaky.

## What was left out

The brief excluded these, and none were built:

- `calibration_list`;
- per-test cards;
- switching presets;
- a hook for returning to the person's project;
- Bambu's automatic calibration.

Also not done:

- **The prompt tests in section 6** were not recorded. They check two things:
  a symptom leads to the two facts and a reply choice before any test is
  made, and a photo leads to one preview and one save. They need a live model
  to answer, and the brief forbids live-model runs without your approval of a
  specific batch. See question 1.
- **No live model was used anywhere.** The in-app conversation was checked
  with a stand-in agent, and the MCP run used a script as the client.
- **Small design gaps:**
  - The Home card menu has no separator above the new row.
  - The "NEW" badge from the boards is not drawn.
  - The filament chip cuts long copy names short ("PLA Basic @BBL A1M · Fake
    A1 mini calibr…").
- **OrcaSlicer's own Calibration menu** in the title bar is unchanged and
  still works the old way.

## Things noticed in the end-to-end run that you may want changed

- **Row label and Undo.** When a test is made over MCP, the chat shows it as
  "Import Object: temperature_tower.drc", with an Undo arrow (e2e shot 02).
  The label is OrcaSlicer's own undo step. The chat's change rows name every
  project change made over MCP that way, so I did not special-case it. Undo
  there would remove the tower from the test project.
- **"Layer time 6 s → 6 s".** After the pressure-advance result is saved, the

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the 27 project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. It is run against the prompt before an edit and after it, and the
counts compared. The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge. `--backend
claude-cli` runs the same cases on the developer's Claude subscription
instead, for iterating on a prompt without API cost (see "Running on the
Claude subscription").

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

A call the app would refuse gets the app's refusal, as ProviderAgent gives
it: a tool not offered on the request is `unknown_tool`, and arguments that
`ToolRegistry::validate_call` does not accept get its own code and message
(`tests/agent/tool_call_check` runs that check, so the runner refuses exactly
what the app refuses, schema rules and the registry's own alike). Every
later call of that response is answered "not run", and the run goes on. A
refused call is never judged, read or change: the case sees only the calls
before it. The app answers two refused calls a turn and fails the turn on
the third (`malformed_tool_call`); so does a run. Before 2026-10-20 the
runner answered such reads from the recording, so earlier counts could pass
a call the app would have refused.
A run's report names every call of the response it ended on. `test_steps.py`
checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and
nothing sent (`python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`).

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`; `slice_report` of the
  active plate (no plate named) and of every plate by its `plateId`;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- a `changedOnly` `settings_search` with an empty query of every object on
  every plate (its own changed settings), given for that object whatever
  `limit` the model passed; Opus 5.5 sends it first in the file-loaded and
  print-this cases;
- `view_render` of every plate, and of the active plate with no plate named,
  in the `iso` and `plate` views, given for that plate and view whatever
  size the model asked for. Only the result's text is kept and replayed: the
  pinned hosts refuse any request that carries an image, so the picture the
  app sends after the result never reaches the model here;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed. A search with `changedOnly` is
  answered only by a recorded search with it, and one without by one
  without; never one with a `cursor`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 22
points takes under three minutes. To keep `requests.json` small (about
3 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer. The first `--backend claude-cli` batch (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-19)
left 10 of 63 runs unobserved, nearly all on two reads DeepSeek V4 Flash

  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for

  `AgentHost::make_agent_request` replays them (calls with their results, a
  result over 16 KiB replaced by the omission note, at most 20 entries), the
  new message as `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` builds it (the
  person's words, then the app's `<print_issue>` and `<workspace>` blocks,
  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load report and its
  developer line, the file-loaded skill and the plate's picture on the
  request that first carries a load report, the print-issues skill on the
  request that carries a chip's message or first shows a slice's new
  warnings, the slice-failed skill on the request that first shows a
  refused or failed slice, the setup skill on the request that first
  carries a recorded or changed purpose or a setup change under one, and
  the live results of this turn's calls with the
  workspace block `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` adds. Arguments that need
  ids take them from the real previous result (`{{result/sessionId}}`) or the

  harness checks the tools equal `project_tools.json` and the instructions

## Running on the Claude subscription (`--backend claude-cli`)

`--backend claude-cli` answers every step with the locally installed Claude
Code CLI in headless mode (`claude -p`), billed to the developer's Claude
subscription instead of a per-token API key. `--judge claude-cli` moves the
judge there as well. Neither needs a key; both need the CLI logged in once
with `claude auth login`. The runner refuses to start a run the CLI would bill
to an API key (`apiKeySource` other than the login).

```bash
tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case advice-infill --runs 1
```

The model defaults to `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium`, both pinned so a
count moves only when the prompt does (`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`,
`--claude-judge-model`). `--claude-keep DIR` keeps each run's session file,
tool list, MCP config and the CLI's event stream for reading afterwards.

### Which backend for what

- **Iterating on a prompt or skill: the subscription.** A strong model
  answering the app's real requests, with real tool calls, shows what the
  prompt itself causes: an ambiguous sentence, a rule two sections disagree
  on, a skill that invites the wrong call. It costs no API money, so it can
  be run as often as the subscription's usage limits allow. Those limits are
  shared with the developer's own Claude Code work; start with one case and
  keep `--jobs` small.
- **Before a release: a small paid run on the app's default model.** The app
  defaults to `gpt-5.4-mini` (the OpenAI provider's default in
  `ProviderProfile.hpp`), which scored about like DeepSeek V4 Flash in the
  printer suite's model table (82 and 79 of 87, `tests/printer_prompt`,
  "Which model"). A strong model
  can paper over an ambiguity a weaker one trips on, so a pass on Opus does
  not show the shipped default will pass. That run needs Kenneth's approval
  like every paid batch.
- **The baselines below** are DeepSeek V4 Flash with the OpenAI judge, except
  the subscription baseline, which is claude-cli's own. A claude-cli count is
  compared only with that one. Changing the judge changes
  what every judged case counts, so `--judge claude-cli` results start their
  own baseline, under the same "confirmed results become the baseline" rule.

### How a recorded request reaches the CLI

`claude_cli.py` turns each recorded request into a CLI run, and
`claude_mcp_stub.py` serves the tools:

- **System prompt**: the rendered prompt, as `--system-prompt`.
- **Tools**: the stub is a stdio MCP server with the case's tools (the 27 of
  `project_tools.json`, or the point's own list), with their real
  descriptions and schemas. Every call the model makes reaches the runner
  through it, and the step rules above apply unchanged: a read is answered
  with the recorded answer, a change ends the run (the runner stops the CLI;
  nothing is answered), a response of reads decides or is answered whole.
- **History**: the request's items before its last turn are written as a
  session file the CLI resumes (`--resume <file>`), so earlier messages,
  calls and results reach the model as its own turns, tool calls and tool
  results, not as a transcript. The last turn's message (the person's words,
  the `<workspace>` block, the plate's picture) goes in as one stream-json
  user message.
- **A point recorded mid-turn**, after a tool result (`after-preview`,
  `after-apply`, `after-slice`, `after-intent`, `direct-change-applied`,
  `direct-change-failed`, `first-person`, `slice-refused-by-tool`): the
  session ends on that turn's last call, marked as a deferred call. The CLI
  runs it through the stub, which returns the recorded result, and then asks
  the model.

Nothing from the developer's own Claude Code setup reaches the model: no
CLAUDE.md, auto-memory, settings, hooks, output style, skills, other MCP
servers or built-in tools, a minimal environment, and an empty temporary
working directory. `test_claude_cli.py` checks that, and the shapes above,
by running the installed CLI against a fake Messages endpoint on localhost
(no login, nothing sent; about 10 seconds). Run it after a CLI update: the
session file is the CLI's internal format, verified against 2.1.283.

What differs from the app's request, beyond the model:

- **Developer messages.** The Messages API has no developer role, so each of
  the app's developer items (its notes after a file-load report, the skills)
  is a user text block wrapped in `<developer_message>` tags. Hosts that
  drop or demote the developer role raise the same question for the API
  backend.
- **The CLI's own text.** Before the prompt, the CLI sends a billing header
  and "You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK."; after
  the first message it adds a short environment note (the temporary working
  directory, platform, date and model name) and an empty system turn
  carrying the effort setting.
- **Tool names** carry the CLI's MCP prefix: the model sees
  `mcp__jusprin__settings_get`, while descriptions, which name other tools
  bare, are unchanged. The runner strips the prefix.
- **Mid-turn points**: after the deferred call's result, the CLI adds
  "Continue from where you left off." as a user message. The app's notes
  that follow the result there (the setup skill in `after-intent`, the
  slice-failed skill in `slice-refused-by-tool`) are further text blocks of
  that same tool result, since the CLI resumes no message after it.
- **Notes sent once** (a point's `once`) stay in the history after the
  first answered read; the app leaves them out of the turn's later requests.
- **Pictures** reach the model, unlike on the pinned DeepSeek hosts, so
  `model-opened-unnamed`, `model-imported-by-tool` and `model-opened-by-tool`
  can be measured here.

The usage the runner logs is the CLI's token count; on the subscription it is
not billed per token.

## Judging a prompt or skill change

What the suite is for (Kenneth, 2026-10-19): showing that a change has not
made the prompt substantially worse. At three runs a case it detects large
regressions only, not small effects. Day-to-day host noise is small next to
what it looks for: on the printer suite the same prompt scored 76, 76 and 74
of 84 on three runs.

1. After a prompt or skill change, run the "after" batch only: the checkout,
   same model, pinned hosts and judge, three runs a case. Compare it with the
   current baseline table below. There is no before run.
2. Judging the result. There are no fixed thresholds (Kenneth,
   2026-10-19). The agent running the batch compares it with the baseline
   case by case and reads every failure and unobserved run. It decides
   whether anything looks like a real regression worth investigating, and
   says why. A case with no baseline row is judged on its own expectation.
   When it is not sure, it asks Kenneth.
3. Only for a case that looks like a regression, run it again with
   `--prompt-rev <previous revision>` the same day. That tells the prompt
   apart from changed requests or a bad host day; a bad host day usually shows
   as drops in untouched cases too. A case run alone gets 20 runs, which is
   what to use before reading a smaller gap as real.
4. Baselines. The current baseline is one section. When Kenneth confirms a
   new result is good enough, it becomes the new baseline, and the old one
   moves to "Baseline history" below, kept for audit only and not used for
   comparison.

result.output:
---
name: calibration
description: Read when a print problem may come from the filament or its settings (stringing, under- or over-extrusion, gaps, bulging corners), when the person asks to calibrate a filament or printer, or when this project is a calibration test or they send a photo of one.
---

# Calibrating a filament on a printer

The rules above still apply. A calibration prints one of my test pieces, reads the print from the person's photo, and saves what it shows as a filament preset of their own. I have three tests: temperature, flow and pressure advance. Each one is a project of its own, made with calibration_generate.

## When a test is worth it

A test answers one question about this filament on this printer. Match it to what the person sees:

- Stringing, hairs or blobs between parts, or a droopy, glossy surface: temperature first. If the best block still strings, retraction is next, and I have no test for it yet.
- Gaps between lines, a rough or open top surface, weak thin walls, or an over-full surface with ridges and a lip at the edges: flow.
- Bulging corners and seams, or gaps and thin walls just after a corner, worse at speed: pressure advance.
- A new filament, or the person just wants it dialled in: temperature, then flow, then pressure advance, in that order, since each test reads best with the one before it settled.

Some problems come first, and a test would only measure them:

- Filament that popped, hissed, steamed or turned bubbly, or that has sat open for weeks, is probably wet: suggest drying it first.
- Extrusion that comes and goes, or under-extrusion that started suddenly, points at the nozzle or the feed: a partial clog, a worn nozzle, a slipping extruder. Ask the person to check those first.
- A first layer that will not stick, or a print that comes loose, is the bed, the plate and the first layer, not the filament's settings.

When none of the tests fits, say so instead of offering one.

## Before making a test

Say two things in your own words and get a reply before calling calibration_generate: the open project will be saved to its version history and closed, and the test opens as a project of its own; the test changes settings only for itself, and nothing is saved to a preset until the person chooses. End with a Choices line, such as "Choices: Make the test | Not now".

When the person's message already says they are fine with the project being saved and closed (a Calibrate… row in the app writes that for them, after showing both facts), they have answered: do not ask again. If they have not said which test, or what they are seeing, ask that instead, with the tests as choices.

The test is made for the printer and filament in use. When the message names a printer that is not the one in use (a Home printer card names only its printer), set it up with printer_setup_preview and printer_setup first, with the filament the person names or the printer's usual one, and only then make the test.

## The three tests

Read the printer, the filament preset and its material from the workspace. Ranges below are mine, and calibration_generate refuses one outside what I accept.

**Temperature.** A tower of blocks, each printed 5 °C cooler than the one below it, labelled with its temperature. start is the bottom block's, the hottest; end the top's; both multiples of 5, start at least 5 hotter. My ranges by material: PLA 230 to 190; ABS and ASA 270 to 230; PETG 250 to 230; PCTG 280 to 240; TPU 240 to 210; PA-CF and PET-CF 320 to 280. Narrow one to the filament's own nozzle_temperature_range_low and nozzle_temperature_range_high when those are tighter (settings_get, filament scope). For another material, centre the range on the preset's nozzle_temperature.
Photograph: the side with the numbers, close enough to read them, in light from one side so strings and droops show. Reading: too hot strings, sags under the overhangs and bridges and looks glossy and blobby; too cold looks rough and dull, bridges poorly, and layers may split. The best block is the coolest one that still bonds and bridges cleanly. It writes nozzle_temperature, and nozzle_temperature_initial_layer kept at the same offset from it the preset had.

**Flow.** Tiles printed at different flow, each with its change embossed on it and in its object name. linear true, the default, is the recommended set, whose tiles add an amount to the flow ratio (-.05 to +.05 on pass 1, finer on pass 2); linear false is the classic set, whose tiles name a percentage change. Start with pass 1; offer pass 2 only when two neighbouring tiles look equally good.
Photograph: the top surfaces from straight above, in light from one side, all tiles in view. Reading: the best tile has a smooth, closed top with no gaps between lines and no ridges or a raised edge. Read filament_flow_ratio with settings_get first: the new value is that plus the tile's amount for the recommended set, or that times (100 + the tile's percentage) / 100 for the classic set. It writes filament_flow_ratio.

**Pressure advance.** method tower, the default, prints a tower whose pressure advance rises by step for each millimetre of height from start at the bottom; line prints numbered lines; pattern prints numbered corners. Leave start, end and step to calibration_generate's defaults unless the person asks; give extruderType bowden for a printer that feeds through a long tube, otherwise leave it. Bambu Lab printers measure this themselves before a print when flow dynamics calibration is on, and the value they measure stays on the printer: say so before offering the test on one.
Photograph: tower: the corners from the side, with a ruler beside it or the height where they look best; line or pattern: from straight above, numbers in view. Reading: the best height or line has sharp corners with no bulge before them and no gap or thin wall after them. For the tower the value is start plus the best height in millimetres times step; for line and pattern, the number by the best one. It writes pressure_advance, with enable_pressure_advance on.

All three write the filament preset.

## After making a test

The test's project opens with my note of what I made. In that turn, call setup_record with the test as the purpose (such as "Temperature test for Bambu PLA Basic") and the range as the headline, then slice it with slice_start. Tell the person to print it, what to photograph and how, and to send the photo here.

When the person comes back to a temperature or pressure-advance test, check its plate in the workspace: while the plate carries calibration, its steps are in place. Without it the test was saved and reopened, which keeps the tower but not its steps, so it would print at one setting: say so, and offer to make it again with the same range before anyone slices or prints it. A flow test keeps its tiles' ratios and needs nothing.

## Reading the photo and saving the result

Name the best block, tile or height and why, and the runner-up. If the photo cannot show it (blurry, too far, the wrong side), ask for another before guessing. Then propose one write: settings_preview_patch on the filament preset in use, with persistAs, then settings_apply_patch with what the preview showed.

The name: when the preset in use comes with the app, save a copy named "<filament preset> · <printer> calibrated", with the printer named as the person named it (such as "Bambu PLA Basic · Prusa MK4 calibrated"). When it is already that copy, from an earlier test, save into it under its own name: never a second copy. When it is a preset of the person's own, ask whether to write the result into it or save it as a copy with that name, and do what they choose.

The test changed some of the filament's settings for itself. When the preview warns saves_unsaved_edits, it lists them with their saved values: put each one you are not writing into the same patch at its saved value, so the preset keeps only the result.

## After saving

Say the preset's name exactly, since the filament menu may shorten it. Say that this test project uses it now, that other projects keep their filament until the person picks this one for them, and that it can be changed back. Then offer the next test in the order above, without starting it.

def judge(log, question):
    """A yes or no about the conversation's last reply, from a stronger model,
    for what no string test can check. Returns (yes, why)."""
    schema = {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": False, "required": ["answer", "why"],
              "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string", "enum": ["yes", "no"]}, "why": {"type": "string"}}}
    instructions = ("You read a chat between a 3D printing app's assistant and a person, and answer one "
                    "question about it strictly as written, judging only what the messages say.")
    prompt = "\n".join(log) + "\n\nQuestion: " + question
    if CLAUDE_JUDGE:
        verdict, usage = claude_cli.judge(instructions, prompt, schema, *CLAUDE_JUDGE)
        count(usage, judge=True)
        return verdict["answer"] == "yes", verdict["why"]
    response = post({"model": JUDGE_MODEL, "store": False, "instructions": instructions, "input": prompt,
                     "text": {"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "verdict", "strict": True, "schema": schema}}},
                    os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"], JUDGE_ENDPOINT)
    count(response.get("usage"), judge=True)

    verdict = json.loads(text)

def readable(item, limit=1500):
    """One input item as a line of the judge's transcript."""
    if item.get("type") == "function_call":

    if item.get("type") == "function_call_output":

"""Merge the cases of a partial recording into tests/project_prompt/requests.json.

The recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide (settingItems),
and an answer's items are indices into that list; the new cases' indices are
moved onto the merged list. Usage: merge_requests.py <requests.json> <partial.json>
"""
import json
import sys

target_path, partial_path = sys.argv[1:3]
target = json.load(open(target_path, encoding="utf-8"))
partial = json.load(open(partial_path, encoding="utf-8"))

items = target["settingItems"]
index = {json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True): i for i, item in enumerate(items)}


def moved(i):
    item = partial["settingItems"][i]
    key = json.dumps(item, sort_keys=True)
    if key not in index:
        index[key] = len(items)
        items.append(item)
    return index[key]


for name, case in partial["cases"].items():
    for answer in case["answers"]:
        if not answer.get("settingItems"):
            continue
        output = json.loads(answer["output"])
        for field in ("items", "unknownKeys"):
            if field in output["result"]:
                output["result"][field] = [moved(i) for i in output["result"][field]]
        # As the recorder writes it: nlohmann's compact dump, keys sorted.
        answer["output"] = json.dumps(output, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
    target["cases"][name] = case
    print(f"merged {name}: {len(case['answers'])} answers")

target["cases"] = dict(sorted(target["cases"].items()))
with open(target_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as file:
    file.write(json.dumps(target, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
print(f"settingItems {len(items)}")

content.text:
I ran the 10 approved runs on DeepSeek V4 Flash (pinned hosts). The assistant always asked before making a test and always previewed the right setting, but the cases passed only 2 of 5 and 0 of 5. The causes were the copy's name, a missing fact, and a flaw in my own symptom check.

**Calibration result (2 of 5 passed).** In the scenario, the person has printed the temperature tower and describes it in words, because the pinned hosts refuse pictures.
- All five runs did the right thing: 215 °C for the nozzle and the first layer, on the filament, as a preview before any save, and into a copy rather than the stock preset.
- The three failures were only in the copy's name. They called it "Bambu PLA Basic · Bambu Lab X1 Carbon 0.4 nozzle calibrated", using the printer preset's name. The skill asks for the printer as the person named it: "X1 Carbon".

**Calibration symptom (0 of 5 passed: 3 failed, 2 couldn't be judged).** The person says their PLA strings and its overhangs droop.
- No run made the test without asking first.
- The two unjudged runs asked for settings the recording doesn't hold, so the test couldn't follow them.
- One failure actually gave both facts word for word and ended with choices, but the facts were in an earlier message of the same turn. My check only read the last message. Since the person sees every message, I changed it to read the whole turn; that version hasn't been run yet.
- The other two left out that the test's settings are its own and nothing is saved until the person chooses. One of them also asked yes or no instead of offering choices.

The batch used 23 model requests (304,272 input tokens, 173,568 of them cached; 8,547 output) and 3 judge calls.

**A gap I had to fix first.** Since the calibration skill was added, every project chat offers the model a `skill_read` tool. The prompt suite's recorded requests were older and didn't include it. I updated the suite to send what the app sends, recorded the two new conversations with the real app on this machine, and merged them in; the 24 existing recorded points are unchanged. The recorder didn't work on Windows because of line endings, so I fixed that too, and it now passes here.

Committed as a63d497e94 (the Windows recorder fix) and 6dfd52a6ed (the two cases and the suite update). The README has the results.

The fix I'd suggest is two wording changes in the skill:
- Use the printer's name the way the person refers to it, never the preset's name.
- Give both facts together, in the message that offers the choice.

Testing that needs another batch of about 25 model requests.

16	- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. 17	- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. The rebuilt app is open on your desktop, with all your requests handled and committed (2bf0d86d4c). Nothing is pushed, and only Windows is tested.

- The app runs on a copy of this machine's settings in `C:\b\calapp-data`, so your normal settings aren't touched.
- It starts with no printers and no AI set up. Add your API key in the assistant panel, and add a printer with "+ Add printer"; you don't need real hardware for the Calibrate rows.

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working but the person cannot see it.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, because the person may not have been watching the pane.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

1	# Handoff: printer and filament calibration in JusPrin
2	
3	Written 2026-10-21 for the agent who implements calibration. Nothing is coded yet; this document records the
4	decisions Kenneth made, the facts verified in OrcaSlicer's code, the design on the canvas, and the smallest build
5	that satisfies both. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` and the documents it lists first; `fork-stewardship.md`
6	governs every line you change outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`. This file is untracked on purpose: never commit it.
7	
8	## 1. What a calibration is, in one paragraph
9	
10	A person has a symptom (stringing, under-extrusion, bulging corners) or just wants a filament dialled in. The agent
11	decides whether a test is justified, generates OrcaSlicer's own test geometry into a project of its own, the person
12	prints it and sends a photo, the agent reads the print, and the result is saved as a new preset whose name the person
13	is told to use from now on. The product definition's section 2.11 lists the eight agent steps; this handoff is how
14	they map onto code.
15	
16	## 2. Decisions already made (Kenneth, 2026-10-21)
17	
18	1. A calibration is a project of its own, as long as the person is told what will happen before their project is
19	   closed. Not a plate in the current project (see fact 1 below for why that is impossible without rewriting Orca).
20	2. First batch: temperature tower, flow rate, pressure advance. Nothing else in this iteration.
21	3. The outcome of every test is a new preset: a named copy of the filament (or of the process or printer preset for
22	   the tests that write there). The app does not switch any project to it. The receipt names the preset and the
23	   agent tells the person to pick it from now on.
24	4. No remembered "return to the previous project". The test project is left through Home like any project.
25	5. No per-test UI. Adding a test must be a declaration plus skill text, not page code.
26	6. The physical-print ledger: "doesn't matter, whatever is the easiest". Leave it alone.
27	7. Entry points are hard-coded: a "Calibrate…" row in the project header's printer chip menu, in the filament slot
28	   menu, and in the Home printer card's kebab. A symptom typed in the project chat leads to the same flow.
29	
30	## 3. Facts verified in the code (read, not run)
31	
32	1. **Every OrcaSlicer generator replaces the open project and edits project-wide presets.** `Plater::calib_pa`,
33	   `calib_temp`, `calib_flowrate`, `calib_max_vol_speed`, `calib_retraction`, `calib_VFA`, the input-shaping pair and
34	   `Calib_Cornering` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp` from about line 12677) each call `new_project()` and then write to
35	   `preset_bundle->prints/filaments/printers.get_edited_preset().config`. Plates have no presets of their own, so a
36	   test on a plate of an existing project would change every other plate. Do not try.
37	2. **The test's parameters are runtime-only.** The generator stores them on the current plate's `Print` with
38	   `set_calib_params` (`Print.hpp:1089`); `GCode.cpp` reads them per layer (temperature at line 4697). Nothing writes
39	   them to the 3MF, and loading a project resets the mode to none at `Plater.cpp:5891`. A saved temperature tower,
40	   reopened, slices as a plain tower at one temperature. The pressure-advance pattern is the exception: its per-layer
41	   commands go into the plate's custom G-code, which the 3MF does save. The PA pattern also hard-codes the first
42	   plate's origin (`Plater.cpp:12814`).
43	3. **OrcaSlicer already treats one outcome as a new preset.** The Bambu wizard's save page writes flow results as a
44	   filament preset named "<filament> Flow Rate Calibrated" (`CalibrationWizardSavePage.cpp:37`). Its pressure-advance
45	   results go to the machine, not a preset. The SoftFever dialogs (`calib_dlg.cpp`) save nothing: the person types
46	   the value into a preset by hand.
47	4. **Saving a copy already exists and selects the copy.** `settings_apply_patch` with `persistAs` saves through
48	   Orca's own `Tab::save_preset` and asserts the copy is now selected
49	   (`Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3356-3369`); the result carries `saved_as`. A stock preset cannot be
50	   overwritten and the preview says so with `read_only_preset` and a suggested copy name (`check_persist`, line
51	   2941). Whether a process-scope copy works end to end is unverified; filament and printer are in use today.
52	5. **Which preset each result belongs to** (from `Preset.cpp`'s option lists): nozzle temperature, flow ratio,
53	   pressure advance, retraction length (as a filament override) and max volumetric speed are filament settings; VFA
54	   writes wall speeds in the process preset; cornering writes junction deviation (process) or jerk limits (printer);
55	   input shaping and Bambu's measured pressure advance live on the machine and produce no preset.
56	6. **The skill mechanism is ready.** `AgentUI/src/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with a `description:` in its frontmatter is
57	   listed to the model and read on demand through the `skill_read` tool (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1209`,
58	   `AgentHost.cpp:2467`). The four skills that exist today are all trigger-based, so this would be the first
59	   on-demand one. Text limit 16 KiB; one skill per directory; name equals directory name (`skillParser.ts`).
60	7. **The project-replacing path already exists.** The `project_open` tool saves the open project to its version
61	   history, drops unsaved preset edits, and calls `m_plater.new_project(true, true, name)` with confirmations skipped
62	   (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2450-2467`, `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1005`). The generate tool should take the
63	   same route, not a second one.
64	8. **The setup card is already data-driven.** `setup_record` (`ToolRegistry.cpp:1071`) titles the pinned card from a
65	   purpose and headline. A calibration project needs no new pinned card: the agent records the test as the purpose
